Emma — thanks for the profile, this is helpful. High level recommendations below; Marcus and Dev are copied to add sizing/cost detail.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Mix: primary pool of H100s for memory-heavy retrieval (pin the large-context LLMs), secondary A100 pool for steady mid-sized workloads, and a small L4 burst pool for short-lived spike handling and caching/preprocessing tasks.
- Why: H100 gives the headroom for large KV caches and long-context models while preserving low tail latency. A100 is cost-effective for steady-state chat where context <8k. L4 is very inexpensive for short-lived generation and batch preprocessing but has smaller memory and lower precision.

Open considerations:
- Do you need strict per-request SLA (p99 latency) for retrieval? If yes, we recommend higher reserved H100 capacity + pinned model versions.
- How tolerant are you for fallbacks to quantized variants (significant cost savings but small quality delta)?

Next steps: Marcus will send a 3-sku sizing matrix with cost/throughput tradeoffs and Dev will propose an autoscale + fallback policy that leverages L4 for bursts. Also attaching a short proposal (proposal_v2.pdf) with our preliminary price bands.

Cheers,

Emma, Irene — dug into the CSV you provided and sketched three scenarios. Numbers below are illustrative hourly cost and effective throughput (tokens/sec) per instance; final pricing subject to contract.

Scenario A — Memory-first (safety-first for retrieval, p99 tight)
- Pool: 75% H100 (80GB), 20% A100 (40GB), 5% L4 (32GB equivalent for bursts)
- When to choose H100: sequences >12k tokens, heavy KV cache usage, models that require FP16/TF32 kernels for perf
- Example perf/cost (per GPU / hr): H100 = $6.40 — 900 tps (large-context), A100 = $3.10 — 520 tps, L4 = $0.80 — 220 tps
- Pros: low p99 for large context; sufficient KV cache. Cons: higher committed cost.

Scenario B — Cost-balanced (mixed workloads, tolerant of small quality delta)
- Pool: 45% H100, 40% A100, 15% L4
- Use quantized A100/L4 variants for non-critical chat; H100 handles retrieval and high-memory work
- Cost (weighted avg): ~35% lower than A

Scenario C — Burst-first (optimize for weekly spikes; smaller base commit)
- Pool: 30% H100, 30% A100 reserved, 40% L4 burst (autoscaled)
- L4 used for pre/postprocessing and ephemeral sessions; stable path has fewer reserved H100s so lower baseline cost but higher risk on p99 during unexpected sustained load

Operational notes:
- KV cache sizing: large-context retrieval benefits from 2–3x memory reservation vs model weights (plan for host-side cache and NVMe-backed cold store for overflow). H100's 80GB grants biggest direct cache.
- Autoscaling: recommend burst policy that first spins up L4 (fast boot), then A100, finally H100. Fallback: quantized A100 variant if H100 not available.
- Canary: a small H100 pilot (3 instances) to validate p99 before full cutover.

I attached an Excel (sku-reco-v3.xlsx) with a per-100k qps break-even analysis and suggested commit tiers. Happy to walk through numbers tomorrow.

Thanks,

Emma — quick ops/implementation notes to make the H100/A100/L4 plan low risk if you sign: 

1) Model pinning & rollout
- Pin the 24k-context retrieval model to H100 pool. We'll do blue/green rollouts with a 3 H100 canary and a rollback policy that shifts traffic to quantized A100 if anomalies detected.

2) Caching & memory ledger
- Implement a memory-ledger that tracks KV cache residency and eviction across pools. Long-lived shards stay resident on H100s; ephemeral shards warm on L4 during spikes and promoted to A100/H100 if stable.

3) Autoscaling config (practical)
- Burst policy: scale L4 by queue depth; if queue depth exceeds threshold for >60s, scale in A100s; if sustained >10 minutes, spin up H100 reserve nodes (subject to billing lead time).

4) Quantization fallback
- Use 4-bit/INT8 for non-critical chat on A100/L4 with automatic quality-monitoring hooks (we can run your evals).

5) Security & tenancy
- All pools in the Dedicated account will run under Helix's VPC. We'll provide separate tenant tags and per-pool metrics in the console for cost attribution.

Next actions:
- Irene: consolidate preferred scenario and commit tier.
- Emma / Procurement: confirm target p99 SLA and acceptance criteria for canary.
- Marcus/Dev: schedule a 30-min walkthrough to show the Excel and autoscaling playbook.

I'll drop the walkthrough invite once we hear preferred scenario.
